argument: Within hidden embeddings of large language models, model scale and layer depth is associated with emergence and contiguous organization of embeddings modulated by theory-of-mind content under ToM-responsive artificial neurons appear in middle and high layers of large models; such modulations are absent in smaller models with chance-level false-belief performance.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported language models, tasks, and embedding analyses; transfer to other architectures or task variants is unestablished.
claim: In large language models, theory-of-mind-related embedding modulations emerge in middle and high layers, are organized in contiguous layers, and are absent in smaller models that perform at chance on false-belief tasks.
conditions: theory-of-mind tasks using true-belief and false-belief trials
comparison across large and smaller language models
falsifier: Probe hidden embeddings across language models of varying scale on false-belief tasks and test whether ToM-related modulations appear only above a scale threshold and in contiguous middle-to-high layers.
interpretation: The evidence supports a empirical association concerning hidden embeddings of large language models.
